Applicant :- Mahadev
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Jitendra Singh,Vipin Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

This application under Section 529 Bnss has been filed with a prayer to direct the court
concerned to expedite the hearing of Session Case No. 607 of 2023, arising out of case crime no. 170
of 2023, under Sections 376 (3), 504, 506 I.P.C. and 5/6 Pocso Act and 67 Information Technology
Act, Police Station- Lalganj, District- Basti pending in the Court of Special Judge Pocso Act, Basti
expeditiously within a stipulated period.

entities.text: Court of Special Judge Pocso Act, Basti
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that in the aforesaid criminal case charge sheet was filed in the year 2023 and the Court concerned took cognizance thereon.
It is also submitted that only two witnesses have been examined so far.
The trial court is not taking any interest for disposal of the case.
4. I have considered the submissions and perused the entire record.

Mahadev vs State Of U.P. on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33650998/
1 5.

It appears from the perusal of the record that this matter pertains to POCSO Act but the trial court is not taking required interest in disposal of the case which requires speedy trial being a case under POCSO Act.
5. The applicant has made a prayer for expeditious disposal of the aforementioned case in a time bound manner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgement dated 29.2.2024 passed in the case of High Court Bar Association, Allahabad Vs State of U.P and others, (2024) 6 SCC 267 has held as under :-
"Constitutional Courts, in the ordinary course, should refrain from fixing a time-bound schedule for the disposal of cases pending before any other Courts.

entities.text: High Court Bar Association, Allahabad Vs State of U.P and others, (2024) 6 SCC 267
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Constitutional Courts may issue directions for the time-bound disposal of cases only in exceptional circumstances.

The issue of prioritising the disposal of cases should be best left to the decision of the concerned Courts where the cases are pending; and"
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has not shown any exceptional circumstances to issue direction for time bound disposal of the present case at this stage.

However, in view of the aforesaid, the present application is disposed of with a direction to the court concerned to decide the aforesaid case expeditiously without granting unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
7. The present application is accordingly disposed of with the aforesaid direction.
